claims.statement: The team Members tab is a navigation entry identified by text and a screenshot caption. It is not an inspected image, complete membership list, accepted invitation, inherited access grant or verified permissions.
The new-team flow asks for the team's name. This is not a concrete identity, validated name uniqueness, generated slug algorithm, completed creation or authority to create or rename a team.

The team Settings tab is identified by navigation and a caption, not image inspection. Reaching settings is distinct from current values, edit permission, completed mutation or enforced configuration.

The Team visibility selector asks for a visibility choice without enumerating options or effects. It does not establish public versus organization-visible semantics, repository visibility, actual selected state or a mandatory local visibility policy.

The organization's Teams tab is identified by text and a screenshot caption. This fragment now receives its own full-file disposition, unlike earlier contextual includes; it still proves neither inspected image, complete team census, nesting, membership nor effective grants.

The Access-sidebar Team discussions entry is documented, but the separately reviewed same-pin team-discussions-deprecation fragment labels Team Discussions retired across FPT/GHEC/GHES branches. This navigation/retirement tension remains explicit and requires containing version/context or published-content reconciliation; navigation is not proof of active support or grounds to resurrect retired features. No setting or discussion migration was performed.
